svg.text: The essay funnels a wide worry about conscious AI into three psychological biases that converge on 'it's
pareidolia,' then into four independent arguments that converge on 'functionalism is shaky,' then forks into two
distinct ethical risks, before looping back to its opening warning that mistaking machines for us means…

g.text: Two converging clusters (why we're tempted; why we should doubt it) lead into a fork of distinct risks, which closes by

g.title: Could AI really be conscious? — and why it would matter — Consciousness brings moral status; getting this wrong distorts ethics either way. — → spya-e68t9h
Anthropocentrism & exceptionalism — human traits as the template — Three overlapping biases make us see human qualities as definitional. — → spya-cvaqgs
Fluent language reads as feeling — 'hallucinate' vs 'confabulate' — LLMs pull our strings via language; AlphaFold doesn't, though it's similar under the hood. — → spya-k6fpme
Exponential hype & techno-rapture — every point feels like a threshold — Exponential curves and dreams of digital immortality inflate expectations. — → spya-cke6sj
g.text: every point feels like a threshold

g.title: Mostly pareidolia — but that's only step one — Recognizing the bias doesn't settle whether real artificial consciousness is possible. — → spya-k850tu
Assumes: computation = consciousness — computational functionalism — The whole case for conscious AI rests on this usually-unexamined assumption. — → spya-d3g67c
Brains aren't software on hardware — No clean separation of mindware and wetware exists in real brains. — → spya-sk4su6
Other dynamics beyond Turing computation — Continuous, analogue, and dynamical processes may matter more than algorithms. — → spya-affgsh
Life itself may be necessary — Consciousness may be tied to self-sustaining, living, predictive bodies. — → spya-e7jqx4
Simulating a mind ≠ creating one — A simulated storm doesn't get anything wet; mind-uploading assumes its conclusion. — → spya-cqh5wq
Functionalism looks shaky, not impossible — Each argument stands alone but together they weaken the case for conscious AI. — → spya-uzr60x
Given the uncertainty, don't build it — Deliberately creating conscious AI would risk new, uncontrollable suffering. — → spya-e7fdmb
If AI really is conscious: disaster — new suffering, hard to switch off — Rights would make dangerous systems harder to control or shut down. — → spya-vs0vpj
g.text: If AI really is conscious: disaster
new suffering, hard to switch off

g.title: If it only seems conscious: illusion persists — no test can settle it — Like a visual illusion, the feeling of AI consciousness survives knowing better. — → spya-gwz5eu
g.text: If it only seems conscious: illusion

g.title: Recover a soul that's more breath than machine — embodied, not disembodied rationality — Mistaking algorithms for minds means overestimating them and underestimating ourselves. — → spya-zv36xq

g.text: WHY WE'RE TEMPTED TO SEE IT
One conflation (intelligence with consciousness) branches into three biases, each with its own mechanism, all
converging on the same conclusion: this is pareidolia.

g.title: Intelligence is doing; consciousness is being — Nagel: 'something it is like to be' an organism — a different property from problem-solving. — → spya-nj888h
Anthropocentrism: human as template — Taking the human example as definitional rather than one case among many. — → spya-h4mwb2
Exceptionalism & anthropomorphism — Placing humans atop every hierarchy, then projecting human traits onto machines. — → spya-her4zk
Language especially triggers belief — LLMs, not protein-folders like AlphaFold, get called conscious — because they talk. — → spya-k6fpme
'Hallucinate' implies felt experience — Better word: 'confabulate' — doing, not experiencing. — → spya-t29n67
Exponential growth feels imminent — On an exponential curve, every point feels like an inflection point. — → spya-cke6sj
Techno-rapture: Promethean immortality — Ex Machina: 'that's the history of Gods' — the lure of building minds forever. — → spya-v4sduf
Silicon Valley incentives amplify it — Magical AI narratives help justify valuations and salaries too. — → spya-mcaa4g
Recognizing pareidolia is only step one — Seeing why we're fooled doesn't yet tell us whether artificial consciousness is possible. — → spya-k850tu

g.text: One assumption feeds four independent two-step arguments — Turing brains, alternative dynamics, life, and simulation —
that converge on the same shaky conclusion.

g.title: Assumption: computation suffices — Computational functionalism, so ingrained it's rarely recognized as an assumption. — → spya-wepmnr
Turing: software is hardware-independent — A universal Turing machine can run any algorithm on any suitable substrate. — → spya-cf70dt
But brains have no such split — What a brain does and what it is cannot be cleanly separated. — → spya-b0086e
Continuous, stochastic dynamics exceed algorithms — Electromagnetic fields, neurotransmitter flux — none strictly Turing-computable. — → spya-n393ru
Watt's governor: regulation, not computation — A 'computational' version of the governor would misunderstand what's going on. — → spya-sq9v5k
Perception as controlled hallucination — Conscious experience as the brain's best guess, calibrated by sensory signals. — → spya-xhvztm
Self-sustaining life grounds prediction — Prediction-error minimization is inseparable from the materiality of metabolism. — → spya-vys3vj
A simulated storm doesn't get you wet — Simulation lacks the causal powers of the thing simulated. — → spya-npjt4j
Mind-uploading assumes its own conclusion — You're no more likely to exist in the sim than a hailstorm is to arise in a weather computer. — → spya-xvm37k
A strong, shaky assumption — Four independent lines each weaken computational functionalism, and together they compound. — → spya-uzr60x
